Eyre. This is a frozen HTML parse of primary article excerpts, not a complete paper: supplied text ends at parse L1240 in Study 1 results and has overlapping retrieved sections. No PDF supplied. Findings of absence apply only to the inspected supplied sections. Replication and unassigned fields are placeholders. The supplied methods give recruited participants by gender, not explicit final analytic group counts for this outcome/test. The explicit shame/guilt models report denominator df 154, whereas manipulation checks report 156; no missing-data/exclusion account or explicit analytic N is supplied. Do not infer analytic N from df or promote recruitment to analytic N. Recruitment arithmetic 87 + 81 = 168 describes contributors only, not an accepted final analytic sum. Description and p. 6 locator leave several distinct tests: shame Public Exposure × Moral Beliefs interaction F(2,154)=3.15, p<.05; publicity simple effects within high beliefs F(2,73)=7.85, p<.001 and low beliefs F(2,73)=6.85, p<.005; moral-belief simple effect in implicit public F(1,57)=11.05, p<.005; mixed Emotion × Public Exposure × Moral Beliefs interaction F(1,154)=3.31, p<.05 (df retained as printed).
